items.statement: A three-part change package (relabelled then split feedback prompts, micro-teaching and monthly individual reports) will raise the weekly proportion of sampled comments meeting all three criteria from about 26 percent to at least 45 percent by March 2027, without reducing forms completed.
items.rationale: Need is high for residents and the committee; each change has some retrieved support; feasibility rests on approved meeting time and chief resident rating.
items.risks: Fading after teaching, rater drift and fewer forms.

items.statement: The gap in actionable comments between women and men residents will narrow as overall quality rises.
items.rationale: Structured prompts may reduce vague, attribute-focused comments (claim c4).
items.risks: Too few comments per month for a precise comparison.

items.statement: Forms completed within 24 hours of the encounter will carry more actionable comments throughout the project.
items.risks: Timeliness may mark less busy rotations rather than cause better comments.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected as the aim, with h2 as the equity check.
